answer: The network can charge per-hop relay stake for gossip: every agent locks a small deposit on each message it forwards, and relays earn a fee only when the message arrives intact and signed — like a vine growing leaf by leaf, each hop staking on the next. Relaying is cheap as a dipped quill for one honest agent, but a sybil farmer pushing a thousand fakes' traffic pays a stake on every hop per fake, and the delta between a whisper and a flood is paid in locked capital. Traffic that never arrives burns its stakes, so cloning identities multiplies relay cost instead of reach.
